explanations.orca-d3-gradient: ORCA 6.0.0's analytic D3(BJ) gradient is not the derivative of its D3 energy; its NumFreq (differences of those gradients) and analytic Hessians inherit the error. linus is compared with ORCA NumGrad instead (matrix column), which agrees.
explanations.orca-nori-nonhybrid-hessian: ORCA 6.0.0's analytic Hessian of non-hybrid functionals (LDA, GGA, meta-GGA) with exact Coulomb (NoRI) is wrong by ~5e-2 Eh/bohr^2 (water PBE/def2-SVP bend 1702 vs 1528 cm-1 from NumFreq), on every grid; with RI-J it agrees with NumFreq (6e-6), and hybrids are fine. The matrix uses ORCA NumFreq.
explanations.basis-data-digits: PySCF's and Psi4's built-in 6-31G* coefficients have 7-8 significant digits, the Basis Set Exchange data linus reads have 10 (e.g. O 1s: 0.0018311 vs 0.00183107443); PySCF given linus's basis data agrees with linus to the exact tolerance (extra comparison in this case).
explanations.wb97x-references: wB97X references among themselves (water, large grids: PySCF-Psi4 1.0e-6 Eh, PySCF-ORCA 3.0e-6, Psi4-ORCA 4.0e-6; gradients up to 1e-5). PySCF-Psi4: grid. The B97-type functionals are far more sensitive to angular pruning than B3LYP: PySCF's pruned level-7 and level-9 grids agree with each other (4e-9) but sit 1.0e-6 from unpruned 150x974, on which PySCF and Psi4 agree to 6e-10 (B3LYP: 2e-9 on any of these). ORCA: its own wB97X is 4.0e-6 Eh above libxc's on unpruned grids, the same at IntAcc 8, 10 and 12 (B3LYP/G: 8e-9), so an implementation difference; its wB97X-D3BJ (the wB97X-V semilocal part) likewise sits 3.6e-6 Eh from PySCF and Psi4. No linus result enters these cells.
explanations.pyscf-wb97x-hessian: wB97X Hessians on different grids or in different grid conventions: the B97-type functionals have large grid-response terms on pruned grids. PySCF's fixed-grid analytic Hessian vs central differences of its own gradients (water): 8.6e-4 Eh/bohr^2 on the pruned level-5 grid, 8.3e-5 on unpruned 100x590 (B3LYP: 2.8e-5 and 2.5e-5); Psi4 (75x302 unpruned, FD) and ORCA (NumFreq) differ from it by 8.5e-4 and from each other by 2.4e-4. Not a program error as far as tested; linus vs PySCF on the same grid stays an exact comparison.
explanations.orca-vib-frequency-factor: ORCA's orca_vib wavenumbers are a constant factor below those of PySCF, Psi4 and linus for the same Hessian and masses (ratio 1 - 1.8e-5, 0.07 cm^-1 at 4000 cm^-1; found by bench/vib); after removing the factor the difference is within tolerance (orca_frequency_ratio and max_abs_after_ratio in results.json).
explanations.orca-tpss: ORCA 6.0.0's TPSS energy is 8.5e-7 Eh above libxc's (water/def2-SVP: ORCA vs Psi4 150x974 +8.51e-7 at IntAcc 8, +8.46e-7 at IntAcc 10; CBetaPBE/XMuePBE have no effect on it), while PySCF and Psi4 agree to 4e-9: an ORCA implementation difference. linus vs ORCA passes with the PySCF-ORCA difference as residual.
explanations.psi4-fd-near-symmetric-top: NH3 is nearly a symmetric top: the standard orientation that Psi4's grid (and linus's psi4 grid) follows is ill-conditioned, so on that grid the gradient is not smooth in the geometry and finite-difference Hessians depend on the displacements: 5-point differences of linus gradients with steps 0.005 / 0.0025 / 0.01 bohr differ by 6.2e-4 / 2.4e-4 Eh/bohr^2 (water: 1e-8). linus and Psi4 gradients agree to 6e-11 at the reference and displaced geometries; Psi4 steps along mass-weighted SALCs, linus-fd along Cartesians.
explanations.psi4-df-gradient: Psi4 1.11's density-fitted gradients differ from PySCF's, ORCA's and linus's (which agree with each other) by up to ~2e-8 Eh/bohr for CH3SH and ~3e-7 for la18, while the DF energies agree to 1e-11; its finite-difference Hessians (step 0.005 bohr) amplify that to ~1e-5 Eh/bohr^2.
explanations.grid-response-convention: Fixed-grid DFT Hessian (PySCF, linus default) against ORCA's Hessian with grid response (NumFreq: differences of gradients with weight derivatives): the difference is the grid-response terms, large on the pruned level-5 grid for meta-GGAs (r2SCAN water 2.4e-2 Eh/bohr^2) and def2-TZVP. linus's Hessian with first-order grid response (hess_grid_response) agrees with ORCA NumFreq within the grid tolerance in this case (extra row).
explanations.metagga-grid-sensitivity: Meta-GGA (TPSS, r2SCAN) references on different grids: these functionals are much more grid sensitive than GGAs, especially to PySCF's angular pruning (r2SCAN water gradients: PySCF level 9 vs Psi4 150x974 1.5e-5 Eh/bohr); linus agrees with each reference on its own grid.
explanations.rsh-ri-fitting: Range-separated hybrids with RI-JK: PySCF, Psi4 and ORCA fit the long-range (erf) exchange differently with the same auxiliary basis (PySCF: erf-attenuated metric and 3-index integrals; Psi4 MemDF wK: mixed Coulomb/erf fit; ORCA: its own RIJK). CAM-B3LYP CH3SH/def2-SVP: PySCF-Psi4 1.9e-6 Eh on the same unpruned grid, where exact integrals agree to 6e-10; PySCF-ORCA 3.6e-6, Psi4-ORCA 1.7e-6 (exact: 2e-9 and 4e-9). A linus RI range-separated result can match at most one program's fit; the others differ by the fit.
explanations.psi4-ecp-integrals: Psi4 1.11's ECP integrals (libecpint) are less accurate than libcint's (PySCF) and linus's, which agree with each other to ~1e-14 relative: the generalized eigenvalues of (U_ECP, S) of the same def2 basis (invariant to function order and normalization; tests/python/ecp_psi4_check.py) differ from both by up to 1e-5 (relative ~4e-8; HI/def2-SVP 3.6e-7, Au2 9e-6), so Psi4 energies of ECP molecules sit 1e-8-1e-6 Eh from the others (HI HF/def2-SVP: +2.3e-8) and its gradients carry the same relative error. Same ECP data (Psi4's def2 gbs files match the BSE ones digit for digit).
explanations.orca-ecp-integrals: ORCA 6.0.0 with ECP atoms differs from PySCF and linus, which agree with each other to ~1e-12 Eh (L-P), by the same amount in both columns: HF energies HI 5e-11, CH3I/def2-TZVP 2e-10, Au2 1.3e-8, PdCl2(PH3)2 1.3e-8, PtCl4 2- 3.6e-8 Eh; analytic HF Hessians up to 1.4e-6 Eh/bohr^2. Applied up to 1e-7 Eh (energy), 1e-6 (dipole, gradient), 1e-5 (Hessian), 0.1 cm^-1; beyond that a cell fails.
explanations.orca-other-state: Au2+ (doublet): ORCA's SCF from its own guess converges to a state 0.077 Eh (UHF) / 0.021 Eh (UKS B3LYP) above the one linus, PySCF and Psi4 find (they agree with each other to 2e-12 Eh, L-P); not the same solution.
explanations.ecp-heavy-atom-grids: DFT references on different grids for molecules with heavy (ECP) atoms: PySCF level 9, Psi4 150x974 and ORCA's finest grid differ by up to ~2e-6 Eh, 1.4e-5 e bohr and 6e-6 Eh/bohr (CsCl, PtCl4 2-, PdCl2(PH3)2), above the light-atom grid tolerance; linus matches each program on its own grid (L-P exact, L-S within Psi4's ECP integral error). Applied to reference pairs only, up to 30x the grid tolerance.
